what_it_does: Quantum machine learning (QML) requires loading ordinary numerical data — like images or sensor readings — into a quantum computer, a step called amplitude embedding where each number is encoded as the amplitude (size) of a quantum wave. Conventional methods for doing this require very deep quantum circuits, meaning many sequential operations, which introduces a lot of noise and error because quantum hardware is fragile and each operation has a chance of going wrong. EnQode addresses this by first grouping similar data samples together using a clustering algorithm (k-means), computing a representative quantum state for each cluster, and then building short, low-depth circuits that are tailored to the actual quantum hardware — reusing the same circuit structure across all samples in a cluster. This standardization keeps circuit depth and gate count low and consistent, so noise levels stay predictable and low across the whole dataset, improving the reliability of any QML model built on top.
